newsitem.title: UK: NWE gasoline ends firm as barrels go to US, France.
newsitem.headline: NWE gasoline ends firm as barrels go to US, France.

text.p: NWE gasoline prices ended higher on Thursday as traders continued to count up the barrels heading to France and to the U.S. as supplies tighten in Northwest Europe.

Traders said Elf has bought at least 100,000 to 150,000 tonnes total of superplus, premium unleaded and leaded gasoline in the last week to make up for production losses at its three French refineries hit by the eight-day-old strike.

Traders were braced for another spree of French buying if the strike that has shut in about 100,000 barrels per day continues, and a threatened one-day, nationwide oil industry strike is carried out on Tuesday.
The arbitrage also remained open to the U.S. and a 60,000 tonne cargo was confirmed sold late Wednesday out of the U.K. Further details were not available.
One refinery trader said Elf had inquired about supplies but he did not have the prompt availability.
Eurograde barges ended $5 higher at $225/$227 fob ARA, with deals for Rotterdam running refinery material at $226 and $226.50.
Regular unleaded barges ended up about $6 at $220 fob ARA, where the last deal was heard concluded.
Elf said late Thursday that it had made proposals aimed at easing the strike and that unions would consult their members.
But a union official, while confirming consultations would take place on Friday, said a three-hour negotiation session with Elf had failed to address the main issue of jobs.
Claude Henry, coordinator at the moderate CFTC trade union, one of five unions in the talks, said he was not satisfied with the outcome.
The barge market was described as relatively quiet and mostly tracking the interest in cargoes. NWE cargoes were assessed at about $228/$230 cif.
